S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.

subtypes.Reduced Concentration: Unable to pay attention or maintain focus on specific activities like conversation, reading, or watching TV.
subtypes.Indecisiveness: Extreme difficulty making even minor daily choices (e.g., menu, clothes) and hesitating to make decisions.
subtypes.Subjective Memory Complaints: Complaining of memory decline, such as forgetting where things were placed, due to reduced focus.
subtypes.Clouded Thinking: Thinking feels foggy, dazed, or not clear.

S083.name: Hopelessness
S083.description: A feeling of despair or having no hope for the future.

subtypes.Future Hopelessness: The persistent conviction that the future holds no possibility of improvement.
subtypes.Belief in Impossibility of Improvement: The belief that the current situation will absolutely not get better.
subtypes.Helpless Resignation: A state of helplessness and resignation, believing that nothing will change despite effort.
subtypes.Chronic Pessimism: A persistent tendency to view everything negatively and fail to consider positive possibilities.

symptom.disease_info: Persistent Depressive Disorder (dysthymia) is a chronic mood disorder characterized by a persistently low or dysphoric mood lasting at least two years in adults, with no symptom-free periods longer than two months. It often presents with less dramatic but more enduring impairment than major depressive disorder, involving low mood plus associated features such as low energy, poor concentration, low self-esteem, appetite or sleep changes, or hopelessness. The course is typically insidious and long-standing, frequently beginning after stressful life events or in the context of personality and environmental vulnerabilities, and can coexist with superimposed major depressive episodes ("double depression"). It is distinguished from normal sadness or adjustment reactions by its duration, pervasiveness across life domains, and associated functional impairment, and from major depressive disorder by its chronic, more subtle, and trait-like presentation.

patient.stressor: John’s low mood began shortly after he graduated high school and started working full‑time as a medical assistant instead of following his friends to college, a decision driven by finances and family expectations. What he assumed would be a temporary, practical step became an ongoing routine of early shifts at the rural clinic, evening DIY projects, and solitary gaming, and over the next two years he increasingly compared himself to peers posting about campus life and internships, questioning whether he had already limited his future. As he juggled work, night classes toward an associate degree, and volunteer health fairs, he noticed himself falling behind on coursework, abandoning guitar practice, and avoiding basketball games because he felt mentally "checked out" and unable to make decisions about his next steps. He finally accepted a referral from a nurse practitioner at the clinic—who noticed his growing indecisiveness about even simple tasks and his stalled plans for further training—after he admitted he’d been feeling this way for "a couple of years" and couldn’t seem to get his focus or drive back.
patient.chief_complaint: “For the last couple of years I just can’t think clearly or make up my mind about anything, even simple stuff.”

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.
S024.manifestation: Most days at the clinic and even when I’m home, there’s this steady, heavy feeling like a gray cloud sitting on my chest, and even when something good happens—like a patient thanking me or my friends sending college pics—I just feel kind of empty and left out instead of happy for them.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.
S029.manifestation: No matter how much I sleep, I wake up already wiped out, and just doing a normal shift, then trying to drag myself to night class, feels like I’m moving through mud with zero energy left for stuff I used to like, like playing guitar or shooting hoops.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.
S031.manifestation: It’s like my brain is stuck in low gear all the time—at work I catch myself staring at the computer because I can’t focus on simple charting, and even choosing what to eat after my shift or whether to sign up for another class can take me forever because I go back and forth until I just give up.

S083.name: Hopelessness
S083.description: A feeling of despair or having no hope for the future.
S083.manifestation: When I think about the future, I just see myself still stuck in this same job in this same town while everyone else moves on, and it honestly feels like no matter what I try—more classes, volunteering, whatever—nothing is really going to change in any meaningful way.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: Because I’m so drained and indecisive all the time, I’ve started turning in night-class assignments late, my grades have slipped, and at the clinic I move slower and need coworkers to double-check simple tasks, so I’ve stopped volunteering for extra responsibilities or making plans with friends.
add_requirements.duration: This has been going on pretty much since right after I graduated high school and started working at the clinic instead of going to college, so a little over two years now.
